items.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024
items.q: I guess when Tommy Dorsey died.

ctx.x: That’s a great story. When we see movies about Vietnam now, usually the soundtrack are tunes from pop radio that were occurring during the Vietnam War — Sly & the Family Stone and that kind of thing. Yet you’re saying that these young men were responding to music that had more to do with their parents than it did with them.

Right. Yeah that was in 60- — I started in 1969 until Bob Hope’s last trip which was in ’72. He did ’69, ’70, ’71 and ’72. And you know the big band era, it started to fold I guess when Tommy Dorsey died. I did get a chance to work with Bob Crosby but he wasn’t a big band then, but he was an old guy, an old band. But the bands were still working pretty well. Les Brown was working well, the road bands — you had road bands out there like Ray Anthony. And you know Ray Anthony is still alive. He’s 102, and I used to…
I thought of the guy who you were trying to mention, I think was it Ted Lewis?
